card.hook: Picture a whole building dressed in gold, sitting on an open square like it knows you're coming with your phone. That's the House of the Blackheads, and you can fit the entire front in one shot.
card.stand_here: Stand in the middle of Rātslaukums (Town Hall Square), about 10 m south of the façade, and face north toward the building. Stay in the open square so the whole front fills your screen.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the classic straight-on view. Try 0.5x if you want more of the square, or the spire of St Peter's Church poking up above the gable. If the square is busy, zoom 2x helps you pick out the gilded details above the crowd.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the gable on the middle line, then tap the gilded part of the façade and slide it a touch darker so the gold keeps its detail.
card.best_time: Go in the hour before sunset, when the sun brings out the gilding. The façade is in shade for most of the day. Summer weekends are very crowded, and the Christmas market fills the square with stalls from late November to early January.
card.selfie_here: Stand beside the Roland statue in the square, with the Blackheads façade behind you. Use the front camera and a close-up. The statue sits in front of the building, so the façade fills the background without a wide frame.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand near the middle of the square, about 10 m south of the façade and facing north, while you stand with the façade behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: You can photograph the façade for free from the open square. The museum inside is a ticketed visit, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Get the whole golden front in your shot with St Peter's spire peeking over the gable, and keep the sides of the building dead straight.
card.good_to_know: The building began in 1334 as a warehouse and meeting place for merchants. From the mid-15th century it was home to the Brotherhood of Blackheads, a guild for unmarried merchants, shipowners and foreigners. It was wrecked in June 1941 and pulled down in 1948, then rebuilt between 1996 and 2000, and more than 5,000 people paid to place a brick in the wall. The site is also linked with the first decorated Christmas tree, put up in 1510.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in the middle of Rātslaukums (Town Hall Square), about 10 m south of the façade, and face north toward the building. Stay in the open square so the whole front fills your screen.

card.hook: You're about to photograph a food market whose roofs were once built for airships. The five long pavilions reuse the metal frames of German Zeppelin hangars, so the buildings are as much the show as the produce.
card.stand_here: Stand on Akmens tilts (Akmens bridge), about 567 m and roughly 9 minutes on foot from the middle of the market. Walk south-east and the pavilions will come into view ahead of you. Face the market across the water, and you'll get the Old Town and modern left-bank buildings, the railway bridge and the National Library in the same frame.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x for the pavilion roofs and the long rows of buildings. Switch to 1x for stalls and street scenes. Try 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) for details on stalls from a polite distance.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line up the long pavilion roofs with a horizontal line, then tap the brightest part of a stall and slide it a little darker so the colours stay rich.
card.best_time: Go in the morning, when the stalls are likely to be busiest and fully stocked. Check the official site for opening times before you set off.
card.selfie_here: Try the canal bank beside the market halls on the Nēģu iela side, where the buildings are reflected in the water behind you. Use the front camera at 0.5x and tuck the pavilions over your shoulder. It's based on photos of the reflections rather than a marked spot, so check it when you're there.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by on Akmens bridge to shoot you with the market and railway bridge across the water behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: The market is a known pickpocketing hotspot, so keep a hand on your bag. Ask before photographing a stallholder close up, and check the official site for any rules inside the pavilions.
card.challenge: Find the most colourful pile of produce you can, then take one wide shot of the roofs and one close-up of that pile, and see which one you like more.
card.good_to_know: The pavilions were built between 1924 and 1930. The market covers about 72,300 square metres and has more than 3,000 trade stands, and it is described as Europe's largest market and bazaar. Together with Old Riga, it has been on the UNESCO World Heritage list since 1998.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Akmens tilts (Akmens bridge), about 567 m and roughly 9 minutes on foot from the middle of the market. card.hook: Picture a slim stone column with a green-copper woman on top, holding three gold stars up at the sky. Locals call her Milda, and you can spot her from right across the canal.
card.stand_here: Stand in Operas skvērs (Opera Square), on the canal side. The monument is to the north of this spot, about 140 m away, so face north with the water in front of you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x so the column, the canal and the plantings all fit in. Then try zoom 2x or more, depending on your phone, to pick out Milda and the top of the column. Zoom 0.5x only if you want lots of foreground, because it makes the monument look small.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the column on a vertical line and keep the phone level, so Milda stands tall instead of leaning.
card.best_time: The guard changes on the hour during the day and people gather for it, so expect a crowd then. If you want a calmer shot, take it between the changes.
card.selfie_here: Try the lime-tree avenue on Brīvības bulvāris, where the trees frame the monument, or the park hill above the cascades in Bastejkalna Park, north of the monument, for a higher view. Use the front camera, and try 0.5x to squeeze more in with the monument over your shoulder. Check the framing on the spot, as the monument can end up small behind you.
card.ask_someone: Hand your phone to a passer-by and ask them to stand a few steps back along Brīvības bulvāris from the column, where the whole monument fits in the frame, while you stand with the monument behind you, keeping a respectful distance from the guards.
card.rules_and_safety: Keep a respectful distance from the guards and keep your voice down, especially at the hourly guard change.
card.challenge: Can you get all three gilded stars in one shot with Milda? Zoom in and count them.
card.good_to_know: The monument honours soldiers killed in the Latvian War of Independence (1918–1920) and was unveiled in 1935. It's 42 metres tall, built of granite, travertine and copper, and paid for by private donations. Milda's three stars stand for Vidzeme, Latgale and Courland. On 14 June 1987 about 5,000 people gathered here to lay flowers, a moment that helped renew the independence movement.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Operas skvērs (Opera Square), on the canal side. The monument is to the north of this spot, about 140 m away, so face north with the water in front of you.

card.hook: You'll spot that big brick tower long before you reach the square, and it's the one everyone wants a picture of. The trick is finding room to fit all of it in.
card.stand_here: Stand in Doma laukums, the square in front of the cathedral's west facade. Face the cathedral so the whole brick facade and tower fill your screen, with the cafés and people at its base.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for the full facade and tower. If the square is busy and you can't step back far enough, go to 0.5x. Then try 2x or more (depending on your phone) for the tower top, the weathercock and the brickwork.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and keep the tower on a vertical line so the walls don't lean, with a little space above the tower and some café tables or people at the bottom.
card.best_time: Go before 8 am for an almost empty square, or after 4 pm when the light softens. It's busiest from about 10 am to 3 pm, and in December the Christmas market can block views and crowd the square.
card.selfie_here: Take it on the cobbled Doma laukums, right in front of the cathedral, with the facade behind you. Use the front camera, try 0.5x if your phone has it, and let the brick walls and tower rise over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Hand your phone to a passer-by, stand with the cathedral behind you, and ask them to step back across the square so the full tower and facade fit in the shot.
card.rules_and_safety: The square is free and open. The cathedral is a working church, so check the official site before you go inside.
card.challenge: Zoom in and find the weathercock on top, then get a shot of it with nothing else in the frame. Bonus points for a clean, straight tower.
card.good_to_know: Bishop Albert founded Riga Cathedral in 1211, and it's considered the largest medieval church in the Baltic states. It's formally the Cathedral Church of Saint Mary. The copper roof over the nave was replaced in 2011 and the tower was re-plated in 2015, so it's looking sharp.

card.hook: Picture a short brick tunnel with a bright rectangle of street glowing at the far end. That's the Swedish Gate, and it's a photo that looks clever with almost no effort.
card.stand_here: Head for Torņa iela 11 in Riga's Old Town, where the phone icon on the map marks the gate itself. Stand in the passage and face the street at the far end, so the brick walls close in on both sides.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for a straight view through the arch. Switch to 0.5x if you want the full curve of the brick and the street ahead, and keep your phone level so the walls don't lean.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the middle of the arch on the centre line, then tap the bright end of the passage and slide it a little darker so the street doesn't wash out.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning. Tour groups often pass through and block the view, and the street is likely to be emptier before they arrive.
card.selfie_here: Try the Torņa iela pavement, where the yellow Jacob's Barracks runs alongside the arch. Use the front camera, try 0.5x, and hold it so the gate is over your shoulder. Nobody has confirmed a selfie works here, so check the frame on the spot.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the opposite side of the street while you stand at the gate, so they can fit its full height behind you (daylight is best).
card.rules_and_safety: The gate may not be open to walk through, so be ready to shoot from just outside the archway looking in. Be mindful of pedestrians, and be patient if a tour group is passing.
card.challenge: Get both brick walls perfectly balanced around that bright street rectangle, then take a second shot from Torņa iela with the yellow barracks beside the arch.
card.good_to_know: The gate was built in 1698 as part of the city wall, to give access to barracks outside the town. It's the only one left of Riga's former eight gates. There's a local legend about a girl who met a Swedish soldier here in secret, which makes a great caption.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Head for Torņa iela 11 in Riga's Old Town, where the phone icon on the map marks the gate itself. Stand in the passage and face the street at the far end, so the brick walls close in on both sides.

card.hook: The best seat for Riga's Old Town skyline is in a library, and it's not on the top floor. The National Library, nicknamed the Castle of Light (Gaismas pils), has a trick up its sleeve.
card.stand_here: Go inside and head up to the Level 3 seating area. The phone icon on the map is at the library itself. Pick Level 3 over the very top floor, then face the windows for the Old Town, the Stone Bridge and the Daugava.
card.zoom: Use zoom 0.5x for the tiered book shelves and the big interior spaces. Switch to 1x for the window views over the river and Old Town. If your phone has 2x, it picks out single rooftops and spires.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and line the river or the bridge up with a horizontal line, then tap the Old Town on screen and slide darker so the sky doesn't turn white.
card.best_time: Go during the library's opening hours, which vary, so check the official site first. The upper-floor view can close for private events.
card.selfie_here: Stand beside the bronze Divi Raiņi (Two Rainis) sculpture on the forecourt, at the library entrance side on Mūkusalas iela 3. Use the front camera, try 0.5x, and keep the library right behind your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by on the Old Town side of the Stone Bridge (Akmens tilts) to stand facing across the Daugava toward the library on the left bank, while you stand in front of them.
card.rules_and_safety: Reaching the upper floors is reportedly free with a visitor pass, but the outdoor roof deck is reportedly guided-tour only. Check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Get one shot of the tiered shelves with the lines leading your eye in, then walk to a window and line the Stone Bridge up with a grid line. Two very different photos, one building.
card.good_to_know: Latvian-American architect Gunnar Birkerts designed the building in 1989, and it opened in 2014 on the left bank of the Daugava, away from the Old Town. The library itself is much older: it was founded in 1919 as the State Library. Today it holds more than 5 million titles.

card.hook: Picture a big black box dropped into a storybook Old Town of pale stone and spires. That's this museum, and it makes a great photo because nothing else in Riga looks like it.
card.stand_here: Stand in Latviešu strēlnieku laukums, the museum's own square, across from the museum with the tall granite Riflemen Monument in front of you. The subject is to the north-east of you, so face that way.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for the classic view with the monument, the museum and the skyline all in one frame. Switch to 0.5x if you want more of the square and sky, or try 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) for a tighter shot of the monument with the museum behind it.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on gridlines, put the monument on one of the vertical lines, and keep the phone level so the building's straight edges stay straight.
card.best_time: Go in daylight when the sky is bright but not harsh, which suits the dark walls. Early in the day the square is usually quieter, so it's easier to keep people out of your foreground.
card.selfie_here: Stand on the square in front of the museum with the façade behind you, and use the front camera. Try 0.5x if your phone offers it for the front camera, and keep the Riflemen Monument off to the side or out of frame so the black building is your backdrop.
card.ask_someone: Ask someone to stand at the riverside end of the square, in front of the Riflemen Monument, and shoot towards the museum, so the monument is in the foreground with the museum behind it.
card.challenge: Can you fit the monument, the black museum block and St Peter's spire all in one frame without chopping off the spire?
card.good_to_know: The building dates from 1971, when the Soviets put it up to mark what would have been Lenin's 100th birthday. The present museum was founded in 1993 and tells the story of Latvia's occupations between 1940 and 1991. The Riflemen Monument is a Soviet-era memorial that's still debated in Latvia, so it's worth knowing a little of its story when you photograph it.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Latviešu strēlnieku laukums, the museum's own square, across from the museum with the tall granite Riflemen Monument in front of you. The subject is to the north-east of you, so face that way.

card.hook: Your first shot of Riga Castle will probably cut off an end, because this pale, long building is wider than it looks. Don't worry, there's a whole square to back up into.
card.stand_here: Stand on Pils laukums (Castle Square), the open square in front of the castle, and face the castle with the Daugava river behind it. Step back as far as the square allows so the whole front fits.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to squeeze in the whole facade. If you can step well back, zoom 1x looks more natural. Then try zoom 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) for the round towers, roofline and windows.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line the building up with a horizontal line, so the facade doesn't lean, and leave a little sky above the roof.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning or late in the afternoon, when the light is soft and golden. If the sky is bright, tap the facade and slide it a touch darker so the pale walls keep their detail.
card.selfie_here: Climb the green paths of Bastion Hill (Bastejkalns) behind the castle, face away from it toward the city views, and use the front camera with the castle at your back. For a close selfie, try the Swedish Gate beside the castle, where the cobbled street makes a nice frame.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand back on Pils laukums, in the open square in front of the castle, while you stand in front of the building so the whole facade fits behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: The square in front of the castle is open to walk onto. The northern part is the President's residence and the museums are in the southern part, so check the official site before any visit. Personal photos without flash are often allowed in public areas, but check on site.
card.challenge: Find the mix of round and square towers, then get one photo that shows both with you grinning in front.
card.good_to_know: The castle was founded in 1330 and rebuilt between 1497 and 1515, after Rigans destroyed it in 1484. When it was rebuilt, two of the original four square corner towers became round ones. Today the northern part is the President of Latvia's residence and the southern part holds several museums.

card.hook: Here's a street where you spend the whole walk with your chin up. Every building on Albert Street is showing off, with faces, masks and curly stonework at every level.
card.stand_here: Stand on the pavement across the street from Alberta iela 4 and face the entrance arch, so the carved three-faced head is right in front of you. The middle of Albert Street lies to the south-east of this point.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for the head-on shot of the entrance, with the arch centred and the carved head in the top half. Switch to 0.5x to fit a whole building or several facades side by side. Try 2x or 5x (depends on your phone) for the faces and masks.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines so the building edges stay straight when you tilt your phone up, and if the sky washes out the top of the facade, tap the carved stonework and slide it a little darker.
card.best_time: Go before 09:00, when the street is quietest and the north-facing facades get good light in summer. Weekends and 11:00 to 15:00 are busy with tour groups.
card.selfie_here: Head to the corner where Alberta iela meets Elizabetes iela and turn around so the ornate Alberta facades are behind you. Use the front camera, try 0.5x if your phone offers it for the selfie, and let the buildings fill the space over your shoulder. You can also try the pavement opposite the Alberta iela 4 entrance arch, with the decorated street behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: This is a residential street, so keep your voice down, stay on the pavement, keep photo stops brief and don't block doorways. Confirm the house number for Alberta iela 4 on your map before you go.
card.challenge: Find three different carved faces or masks, and get all three in one photo gallery.
card.good_to_know: Albert Street was built in 1901 and named after Bishop Albert, who founded Riga in 1201. Many of the buildings were designed by Mikhail Eisenstein, and Konstantīns Pēkšēns and his pupil Eižens Laube worked here too, so every door looks different. Number 12 was Pēkšēns' own home and has housed the Riga Art Nouveau Museum since April 2009.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the pavement across the street from Alberta iela 4 and face the entrance arch, so the carved three-faced head is right in front of you. The middle of Albert Street lies to the south-east of this point.

card.hook: Here's a small surprise: the best opera photo starts with the fountain, not the opera. The sculpture sits right in front and makes the grand building behind it look even grander.
card.stand_here: Stand beside the ornate fountain right in front of the Latvian National Opera on Aspazijas boulevard; the phone icon on the map marks the spot. Face the building so the fountain fills the foreground and the opera sits behind it.
card.zoom: Start at 1x so the fountain and the opera both fit. If you're too close to get the whole facade in, tap 0.5x. Try 2x or higher (it depends on your phone) to home in on the sculpture or the building's decoration.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and keep the sculpture low in the frame, with the phone held level so the building's walls don't lean.
card.best_time: Soft morning or late-afternoon light flatters both the building and the fountain. After dark, switch on night mode and tuck your elbows into your body to keep the phone steady.
card.selfie_here: Take your selfie at the Fountain Nymph, the fountain in front of the opera's grand entrance, with the opera facade behind you. Use the front camera, and tap 0.5x if you want the whole building over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand in Bastejkalna Park, in the area facing the opera's main facade on the Freedom Monument side, while you pose by the fountain.
card.rules_and_safety: Keep your shots to the outside of the building, as photography isn't allowed during performances. Stay clear of the pavement and entrance so you don't block people arriving for a show.
card.challenge: Get the nymph low in the frame with the whole opera standing behind her, and make every gridline look perfectly straight.
card.good_to_know: The building went up in 1860-1863 as the Riga City Theatre. It burnt down in June 1882, leaving only the outer walls, and was rebuilt in 1882-1887 by city architect Reinhold Schmaeling. The opera company has performed here since 1919.

card.hook: Two cats sit on a yellow roof in Riga with their backs arched and their tails up, and according to the best-known legend, they were put there to be rude to the neighbours. One photo can tell the whole story.
card.stand_here: Stand on Tirgoņu iela, stepped back from the corner toward the Great Guild, across the street. The Cat House lies to the north-east of here, so face that way and get the house and the Guild in the same frame.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the wide shot with both buildings. If the street is too narrow, tap 0.5x. To bring the cats closer, try 2x to 5x, depending on your phone.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines, keep the vertical lines straight so the building doesn't lean, and put the cats on a top third line.
card.best_time: Pick a time when the sun isn't straight behind the cats, so they don't turn into dark blobs against the sky.
card.selfie_here: Use the small open square in front of the Cat House (Meistaru iela 10/12), where the cats are in clear view. Turn your back to the building, use the front camera (try 0.5x if your phone has it), and let the cats peek over your shoulder. The corner of Meistaru iela and Tirgoņu iela works too.
card.ask_someone: Ask someone to stand in the centre of the small square in front of the Great Guild while you stand by the Cat House across the lane.
card.rules_and_safety: The building is private and only the ground-floor restaurant is open to the public, so take your photos from the street.
card.challenge: Make it look like the cats are glaring at the Guild hall, then walk to Meistaru iela and try to spot the second cat on the smaller gable pavilion, which is hard to see from the corner.
card.good_to_know: The Cat House (Kaķu nams) was designed by Friedrich Scheffel and built in 1909, in a medieval style with some Art Nouveau touches. The legend says the owner was refused membership of the Great Guild and had the cats placed with their tails towards the guildhouse, and that they were later turned round to face it. An older version says the quarrel was with the city council and the Town Hall.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Tirgoņu iela, stepped back from the corner toward the Great Guild, across the street. The Cat House lies to the north-east of here, so face that way and get the house and the Guild in the same frame.

card.hook: Three old houses stand shoulder to shoulder on a cobbled Riga lane, and each one looks completely different, like siblings who dressed separately for the family photo.
card.stand_here: Stand on Mazā Pils iela, on the opposite side of the lane, about 10 m south of No. 17. Face the row so Nos. 17, 19 and 21 all fit in the frame, with the cobbles at your feet.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x, which fits the whole row from across the lane. If you can't step back far enough, try zoom 0.5x. Zoom 2x (if your phone has it) is great for the gables or the stone doorway.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and line the houses up with the horizontal lines so the row sits level. Keep your phone upright too, so the gables don't lean.
card.best_time: Early morning, roughly 7:00 to 10:00. The facades catch the sun and the lane is quiet, so you can shoot without tour groups walking through your picture.
card.selfie_here: Use the cobbled lane opposite No. 17, the same spot as the main photo. Switch to the front camera, use zoom 0.5x if your phone offers it, and keep the three houses behind your shoulder. It's a tight lane, so check on arrival that they all fit.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the cobbles across the lane from No. 17, about 10 m south of it, while you stand in front of the houses.
card.rules_and_safety: You can photograph the facades from the public lane. The rear courtyard is reached through the Latvian Museum of Architecture, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Can you get all three rooflines in one level shot, with no one walking through it? Bonus points for spotting the stone doorway on No. 19.
card.good_to_know: Together these are the oldest group of dwelling houses in Riga, and each shows a different stage in how homes were built. No. 17 is the oldest, from the late 15th century. No. 19 has an exterior from 1646 and a stone doorway added in 1746, and No. 21 is a narrow Baroque house. Today they hold the Latvian Museum of Architecture, and they received the European Heritage Label in 2020.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Mazā Pils iela, on the opposite side of the lane, about 10 m south of No. 17. Face the row so Nos. 17, 19 and 21 all fit in the frame, with the cobbles at your feet.

card.hook: Locals call this tower "Stalin's birthday cake", and the second you tilt your phone up at all those stepped tiers, you'll get the joke. It's 108 metres of wedding-cake stonework in the middle of Riga's Latgale suburb.
card.stand_here: Stand right at the Latvian Academy of Sciences, where the phone icon sits on the map. You're very close, so face the tower, hold your phone upright and tilt it slightly up to catch the full height.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to squeeze the whole tower in, then go to 1x for the main body. Try zoom 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) for the spire and the carved details.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and line the tower's edges up with the vertical lines so the sides don't lean in, then tap the building and slide it a touch darker so a bright sky doesn't wash out the stonework.
card.best_time: A clear day with good daylight shows off the stonework and the carvings. At dusk, when the lights come on, switch to night mode and rest your phone against a wall or railing to keep it steady.
card.selfie_here: Try the Island Bridge (Salu tilts): stand on the bridge deck and turn so the Academy tower fills the background, since the building dominates the view from there. Vanšu Bridge is a second option, looking back toward the Academy across the Daugava. Use the front camera (and 0.5x if your phone offers it) and keep the tower over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on Akadēmijas laukums (Academy Square), far enough back to fit the whole building, while you pose in front of the main façade.
card.rules_and_safety: The building can be photographed from outside, but the 17th-floor viewing balcony is a visitor attraction, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Find a hammer-and-sickle sitting next to a Latvian folk ornament and fit both into one close-up. Bonus points if you spot it before your travel buddy does.
card.good_to_know: The tower was built between 1951 and 1961 and was the first skyscraper in Latvia. Its stepped shape follows the Stalin-era skyscrapers found elsewhere in the Soviet Union. The star that once topped the spire was removed after Latvia regained independence in 1991.

card.hook: Look up from the street and you'll see a tall, slim spire poking out over the old-town rooftops, with a gilded rooster on top. Next to it sits a plain modern apartment block, and the two together make a better photo than the church on its own.
card.stand_here: Stand on Skārņu iela, where the church is to the south-west, about 1 minute on foot. Face along the church's front so the apartment block at Skārņu iela 11 fills one side of your shot and the spire rises above it.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x so the whole spire and the apartment block fit in from the street. Switch to 1x for a calmer, less stretched look. Then try 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) to home in on the top of the steeple and the rooster.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and line the spire up with a vertical line so the tower doesn't look like it's leaning.
card.best_time: Dusk or evening is lovely, when the street lights are on. The street looks good at any time of day, though. After dark, switch on night mode and rest your phone against a wall or railing to keep it steady.
card.selfie_here: Hold your phone at arm's length with the front camera and switch to 0.5x so you get more of the scene. Step back until the spire rises over your shoulder, and tilt the phone up a touch so the tip doesn't get cut off.
card.rules_and_safety: Photos inside the church are generally allowed, but skip the flash, especially during services. The tower is windy, so keep a firm grip on your phone and hold onto your hat. Check the official site before you go for visiting arrangements.
card.challenge: Zoom in on the clock and count the hands. You'll find just one, then see if you can get the rooster in the same shot.
card.good_to_know: The church is first mentioned in 1209, and the tower has been through plenty of fires and rebuilding. Artillery fire destroyed it in 1941. Restoration began in 1954, the main works ran from 1967 to 1983, and the interior was finished in 1984. It's a working parish church, and the clock really does have only an hour hand.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Skārņu iela, where the church is to the south-west, about 1 minute on foot. Face along the church's front so the apartment block at Skārņu iela 11 fills one side of your shot and the spire rises above it.

card.hook: Picture a chunky round tower of dark red brick at the end of an Old Town street, with cannonballs stuck in its walls like raisins in a bun. That's the Powder Tower, and it's hard to take a bad photo of it.
card.stand_here: Walk to the north-western end of Vaļņu iela in Riga's Old Town and turn to face the tower. From there it fills the view at the end of the street.
card.zoom: Start at 1x to get the whole tower with the street leading to it. If it won't fit, tap 0.5x. Save 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) for the brickwork and cannonballs.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines, put the tower slightly off-centre, and keep your phone upright so the walls don't lean.
card.best_time: Go early in the day when the street is quieter, so nobody wanders through your shot. Soft light makes the red brick look great.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera and tap 0.5x if your phone has it, so the whole round tower fits. Keep the tower over your shoulder and hold the phone a little low.
card.rules_and_safety: The streets around the tower are open public space. If you want to go inside the Latvian War Museum, check the official site for opening days before you go.
card.challenge: Get up close and find a cannonball set into the brickwork, then take a detail shot of it.
card.good_to_know: The tower was first mentioned in 1330 as the Sand Tower. The version you see now was built in 1650 on the surviving basement of an earlier tower that had been destroyed. The cannonballs in the walls commemorate the Second Northern War.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Walk to the north-western end of Vaļņu iela in Riga's Old Town and turn to face the tower. From there it fills the view at the end of the street.

card.hook: Picture a fortress wall, then picture it gone and replaced by magnolias and a canal. That's Bastejkalns: the ramparts that once stood here are now a hill with a very good view.
card.stand_here: Climb the footpath to the top of Bastion Hill, the small hill in the middle of the park. Face toward the Freedom Monument and the Old Town skyline, with the heart of the park just to the east of you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to get the canal, trees and skyline in one natural frame. Go to 0.5x if you want more of the park's greenery, then 2x or more (depending on your phone) to pick out the Freedom Monument or the Old Town rooftops.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on your gridlines, put the horizon on the upper line so the canal and trees fill the bottom of the picture, and use a branch or the edge of a path as a frame at the side.
card.best_time: Soft morning or late-afternoon light is usually kinder to the greenery and skyline than harsh midday sun. In spring the magnolias and forsythia add colour, and autumn leaves do the same job later in the year.
card.selfie_here: Head to the Love Lock Bridge over the city canal, inside the park. Use the front camera, try 0.5x, and stand so the padlock-covered railings and the park's greenery are over your shoulder. Bastion Hill summit also works if you want the park below behind you.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand a few steps back along the path while you stand at the lookout at the top of the Bastion Hill footpath, so the park and city fall away behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: The park is open to the public, but check the official site before you go for the current state of the canal and hill paths. If the ground is wet or icy, check the hill paths before you climb.
card.challenge: Take a few frames as you walk up the hill, because the view changes with every step. Then pick your favourite and see if you can spot the Freedom Monument in it.
card.good_to_know: The city's fortress ramparts stood here until they were pulled down in 1856, and the grounds were then reshaped into gardens and paths. Landscape architect Georg Kuphaldt was a key figure in the planting. A dolomite waterfall cascade from 1898 still survives, and the park now holds the Freedom Monument and several other monuments.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Climb the footpath to the top of Bastion Hill, the small hill in the middle of the park. Face toward the Freedom Monument and the Old Town skyline, with the heart of the park just to the east of you.

card.hook: Picture a huge cathedral with golden domes, a big green lawn in front and not a single building crowding it. That's the view from the Esplanade, and it's about as easy as a photo gets.
card.stand_here: Stand in the Esplanade, the park in central Riga, and face the cathedral across the open lawn. If you want to get closer afterwards, walk east towards the domes.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to get the whole cathedral across the park. Then try zoom 2x to 5x (depends on your phone) for the golden domes and the facade details. Use zoom 0.5x only if you walk up close and want the whole front in one shot.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the cathedral on the upper third lines and let the lawn fill the bottom of the frame. Keep your phone level so the towers don't lean.
card.best_time: We don't have an official best hour for this one, so if you pass by more than once, take a few shots at different times of day and pick your favourite. The gold looks good whenever you catch it.
card.selfie_here: Wander the paths of the park around the cathedral and stop where the domes are in view behind you. Use the front camera, try zoom 0.5x to squeeze more building in, and hold the phone a little low so the domes stay over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Stand on the pavement outside the cathedral at Brīvības bulvāris 23 and ask the passer-by to step back from the building so the domes fit in the frame.
card.rules_and_safety: Photography isn't allowed inside the cathedral, so keep your shooting to the outside. It's a working place of worship, so check the official site before you go for visiting arrangements. In winter the paths around the cathedral can be slippery, so watch your step.
card.challenge: Take three shots of the same dome at different zooms, then pick the one that looks the most golden.
card.good_to_know: This is the largest Orthodox cathedral in the Baltic provinces. It was built in a Neo-Byzantine style between 1876 and 1883, designed by Nikolai Chagin and Robert Pflug. In the early 1960s the Soviet authorities closed it and turned it into a planetarium. Since 1991 it has been restored, and in 2010 the bell tower and dome were gilded.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in the Esplanade, the park in central Riga, and face the cathedral across the open lawn. If you want to get closer afterwards, walk east towards the domes.

card.hook: Here's a fun one: a medieval spire and Latvia's parliament building are next-door neighbours, and one cobbled lane lets you fit them both in a single shot.
card.stand_here: Stand on Jēkaba iela, the lane beside St James's Cathedral in Old Riga. Face along the lane toward the slim spire, with the Saeima building alongside it.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to squeeze in the cobbles, the spire and the parliament building. Then try 1x for a calmer, less stretched look. For the top of the spire or the doorway, zoom 2x to 5x, depending on your phone.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line up a building edge with one of them, so the spire stands up straight instead of leaning.
card.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light and fewer people in the lane. If it's busy, wait a moment for a gap in the passers-by.
card.selfie_here: Head to Jēkaba iela on the south side of the church, in front of the red-and-white baroque entrance portal. Use the front camera, hold it a little low, and keep that candy-striped door over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on Jēkaba iela across the lane from the cathedral's facade, with the Saeima beside the spire, and have them step back until the whole spire fits in the frame.
card.rules_and_safety: Photos are fine outside service hours and flash isn't allowed. Don't wander around taking pictures during Mass. It's a working place of worship, so dress modestly and keep quiet inside.
card.challenge: Get the spire dead straight against a gridline with the cobbles leading up to it, then sneak in a close-up of that stripy door.
card.good_to_know: The church was dedicated in 1225. Over the years it has served Lutherans, Jesuits and Catholics, and it became the Catholic cathedral after 1923. Popes have visited twice: John Paul II in 1993 and Francis in 2018.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Jēkaba iela, the lane beside St James's Cathedral in Old Riga. Face along the lane toward the slim spire, with the Saeima building alongside it.

card.hook: Here's a funny pairing: a serious Gothic guild hall on one side of the square and the Cat House's rooftop cats on the other. Get both in one frame and the whole picture has a sense of humour.
card.stand_here: Stand in Līvu laukums, at the Cat House end of the square. The Large Guild is about 1 minute on foot, roughly 87 m to the north-west. Face the guild's facade across the open cobbles.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to fit the whole facade. Tap zoom 0.5x if you want the Cat House roof and the guild in the same shot. Go to 2x or more for the windows and pointed gables.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the facade, then slide it a little darker if the sky looks washed out.
card.best_time: Early morning usually means fewer people on the square, and soft or overcast light shows off the stonework evenly. Evening is nice too, but check how the light falls on the facade before you shoot.
card.selfie_here: Take it on Līvu laukums itself, with the Large Guild behind you. Use the front camera, try zoom 0.5x to fit more building in, and hold the phone a bit low so the gables stay over your shoulder.
card.rules_and_safety: The square is open public space, but the building is a concert hall under renovation, so check the official site before you go if you want to go inside.
card.challenge: Can you fit the pointed gables, the tall windows and at least one rooftop cat in a single frame?
card.good_to_know: The current building dates from 1854-1859 and has an English Gothic, Tudor-flavoured look. The guild itself goes back to 1353, when its statute was recognised, and that year counts as its founding. It's one of the oldest public buildings in the Baltic states and the home hall of the Latvian National Symphony Orchestra. Renovation is expected to finish by the end of 2026, so parts of the facade may be hidden or look different from older pictures.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Līvu laukums, at the Cat House end of the square. The Large Guild is about 1 minute on foot, roughly 87 m to the north-west. Face the guild's facade across the open cobbles.

card.hook: Picture a slim brick tower rising over a few trees, with hardly a signpost or parked van in the way. That's St. Saviour's, and it's one of the tidier church shots in Riga.
card.stand_here: Stand on the open ground in front of the street-facing facade, at Anglikanu iela 2a, where the phone icon sits. Face the church so the brick front and the bell tower are right ahead of you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x with your phone upright, so the whole facade and tower fit in one frame. If you're close and the tower won't fit, try zoom 0.5x, but keep the phone level. Then zoom 2x or higher (depends on your phone) for the brickwork, the pointed windows and the top of the tower.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines, line the tower up with a vertical line so the walls don't lean, then tap the brickwork and slide it a little darker if the sky is washing out.
card.best_time: Soft morning or late-afternoon light usually flatters brick best. When you arrive, check where the sun is falling on the facade.
card.selfie_here: Try the quiet square in front of the church on Anglikanu iela. Use the front camera, step back until the tower rises over your shoulder, and try zoom 0.5x if it won't all fit.
card.rules_and_safety: It's a working place of worship, so check the official site before you go if you want to see inside. Photos inside are generally fine for personal use, but skip the flash, especially during services or concerts.
card.challenge: Find a pointed window, then frame it with a bit of tree at the edge of the picture, like the church is peeking out at you.
card.good_to_know: The church was designed by Johann Felsko. The foundation stone was laid in 1857 and it was consecrated on 26 July 1859. In 1973, during the Soviet years, it became a student club, and worship returned after Latvia regained independence in 1991.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the open ground in front of the street-facing facade, at Anglikanu iela 2a, where the phone icon sits. Face the church so the brick front and the bell tower are right ahead of you.
